Has run to a fair level all 3 starts to date, sent off favourite but not threatening when seventh of 15 in maiden at Cork (1m) 6 weeks ago. It may well be significant that stable jockey Luke McAteer is aboard stable's ne
Foaled April 8. 4,500 gns foal, Kameko colt. Half-brother to 5f winner Ghostman and winner up to 1¼m Emma's Letter. Dam, 2-y-o 7f winner, half-sister to useful 1¼m-1¾m winner London Bridge.
Foaled February 18. Ardad gelding. Dam unraced out of smart 1m-12.4f winner Star Lahib.

Foaled April 27. €26,000 yearling, Ten Sovereigns colt. Dam unraced half-sister to smart winner up to 8.3f Eternally. Excellent stable 3-16 with 2-y-o newcomers at the time of writing and he's another well worthy of note

Run to just a modest level on each of his first 3 starts but marked step forward switched to a nursery back on all-weather when second over C&D 7 days ago. Trip appeared to stretch him then but possibilities nevertheless

Foaled March 4. Space Traveller colt. Half-brother to winner up to 7.4f King of The Lions. Dam, 2-y-o 7f winner, half-sister to useful 6f-7f winner Another Romance. Yard's newcomers usually better for a run.
Foaled February 16. 22,000 gns yearling, Phoenix of Spain gelding. Half-brother to winner up to 7f Pembrokeshire. Dam 8.5f winner.
Foaled May 1. $190,000 2-y-o, Galilean colt. Dam lightly raced. Clearly made plenty of appeal in the sales ring so interesting if market vibes prove positive ahead of debut.
Inn Of Court colt who offered little when last of 12 on debut at Gowran (1m, soft) 3 weeks ago. RESERVE.

Inns of Court gelding. Half-brother to several winners, including useful winner up to 7f Dig Two (2-y-o 5f/6f winner). Merely hinted at ability when eighth of 11 in a Listowel maiden (1m) 18 days ago. Likely to be brough

races.name: Alan Bushell Racing Remembers Alan Davies Mares' Handicap Hurdle
races.verdict: SHEEZER DIVA has hinted at promise on all 3 qualifying starts and looks the type to do much better now handicapping for her top yard, so she receives the vote. Getarose and Reel Orange are a pair of credible rivals.

runners.note: Well-bred mare who won a bumper and a mares maiden hurdle for Nicky Henderson last season. Bought by new connections for £8,000 and was ridden too aggressively in a novice hurdle at Cartmel but was already dropping away

Well-related mare has hinted at promise, not beaten far in a slowly-run 2½m Wetherby novice that has produced plenty of improvers prior to finishing midfield in 2m novice on qualifying run. Type to do better now handicap

Fair form on the Flat in Ireland for Jim Bolger. Has yet to fully match that form over hurdles and it made little difference she conceded first run to Getarose at Plumpton on most recent outing, given how decisively that

Has largely been consistent since joining current yard, resuming winning ways at Newton Abbot (2¼m) in May, having to work for it against a pair of unexposed rivals. Shaped as if still in good form from a 5 lb higher mar
Showed more than previously when 7 lengths fourth of 9 in Exeter juvenile run at a stop-start gallop in March but made an unpromising start to life in handicaps at Newton Abbot 3 weeks ago.

Well held all 3 outings over hurdles but did show some ability in an Ascot bumper and is worth a chance to show herself capable of better now handicapping on the back of a breathing operation. Harry Skelton prefers Sheez

Just modest form on Flat (stays 8.5f) for Ralph Beckett but proved a different proposition compared to on her first 2 starts over hurdles when winning a weak mares maiden at Market Rasen (17f) just under a fortnight ago,

Placed in bumpers earlier in her career. Has yet to better poor form over hurdles, though wasn't seen to best effect on second handicap start when fifth of 9 at Worcester (2½m) in May, seeming to pay for a big, 4-wide mo

Dropped a long way in the weights last season and ended the campaign with a promising third at Newton Abbot in April. Made the most of a good opportunity 6 months on at Plumpton (2m) and should remain competitive from a
Displayed some promise in bumpers but has yet to achieve much over hurdles, jumping none too fluently in a first-time hood on handicap debut/sole outing for Barry John Murphy at Ffos Las in May.

Finished closer than previously under Rules when second of 3 in a maiden hurdle at Exeter (2¾m, good) in March, though was flattered by her proximity to the winner, who was completely unextended. Back down in trip for ha

races.name: Northern Ireland On Course Bookmakers Association Handicap Chase (0-100)
races.verdict: MINI GETAWAY gained a deserved first success at Sligo last week and from her very low base, she may well follow up. King Gris looks an interesting contender up in trip for handicap debut over fences, with Three By Two another to consider on reappearance.

runners.note: Doubled his tally with an easy victory in 2½m handicap hurdle at Wexford in August last year. Friendless in the betting back over fences for new yard at Ballinrobe and ran no sort of race.
Off the mark in handicap hurdle at Wexford (3m) in May. Disappointing in 2 starts over fences since, in blinkers when well held at Kilbeggan (3¼m) 7 weeks ago, so bounce back called for.
Fairly useful chaser at best but saw her form tail off over the course of last season. Off 8 months but has gone well fresh in the past so market may well be revealing from this handy mark.

Won first 2 starts under Rules, including over C&D but that was back in 2023. Creditable fifth of 15 in handicap chase at this course (23f, soft) 21 days ago, left poorly placed how the race unfolded.

Long-standing maiden who hit the frame on 8 occasions in a row over both sets of obstacles. Didn't seem to see out 3m when snapping that sequence in August and now reverts to chasing with cheekpieces back on.

Managed to win a couple of handicap hurdles around 2½m at Ayr and Hexham last season and very much looks to be being brought along with similar intentions over fences based on his 2 previous efforts in this sphere. Looks
Veteran who has enjoyed an excellent summer, winning 3 times and placed on 4 other occasions, but a busy spell has seemed to catch up with him the last twice.

Maiden hurdler who didn't show much first 2 starts over fences having switched to the larger obstacles late in his career but in a change of headgear, he did offer a bit more when fourth over 23f here 3 weeks ago.

Second to subsequent winner Ladies Well on return reads positively in the context of this race. Not as good back hurdling since though and also put in a moody display back chasing at Sligo last week. Visor replaces blink

Progressive form from her low base over fences, shedding her maiden status at Sligo last week, showing a good attitude in the process. Fourth-place finisher in that race has won since so holds very sound follow-up claims

Long-standing maiden who ran well when second in a 15-runner handicap at Down Royal in August, with the form boosted by the third winning since. However, he underlined his inconsistency since and this a belated second tr
Long-standing maiden who was keeping on in fourth (albeit unlikely to trouble the first 2) when falling at Kilbeggan in August. Jumping fell to pieces at Sligo last week, though. New headgear tried.
Snapped a losing run of over 8 years when landing a 15-runner handicap at Down Royal in April. That race panned out well for him, though, and he wasn't in the same form at Downpatrick soon after.
Fair cross-country chaser who looked very rusty on return in a handicap chase at Ballinrobe and was never a factor over hurdles 3 weeks ago (19f). Back up in trip.

races.name: Darley EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
races.verdict: NEWS looked potentially useful when bolting up first time out at Southwell last month and with improvement on the cards, George Boughey's filly gets the verdict to defy a penalty. Lily Pink got back on track last time, but she may have to settle for a third silver medal from 4 outings, while Watch Party is also respected with this step up to 1m expected to suit. Of the newcomers, Red Curry makes m

runners.note: Cracksman filly who looked potentially useful in making a taking winning start in 10-runner maiden at Southwell (7f) last month, picking up to good effect once she got the hang of things in the straight and shooting clea
170,000 gns Nathaniel filly who is bred more for stamina than speed but showed some ability while shaping as if better for the run when ninth of 10 in maiden at Ascot (1m, good) on debut 5 weeks ago.

Foaled April 9. €30,000 yearling, €65,000 2-y-o, Starspangledbanner filly. Half-sister to 3 winners, including very smart 1½m-2½m winner Coltrane and winner up to 1¼m Warda Jamila. Dam unraced. Big outsider on debut.
Again sent off huge odds and ran to a similar level as on debut when fourth of 9 in maiden at Southwell (1m) last month. One for handicaps later on.

Cracksman filly who made a promising start when second at Newmarket (1m) in August and quickly put a lesser effort behind when again finding only one too good back at Newmarket (1m) last month. Will be suited by longer t
Foaled March 29. Lope De Vega filly. Half-sister to 3 winners, including 1¼m winner Symbolic Power and 2-y-o 6f winner Game And Set. Makes plenty of paper appeal for her top yard.
Foaled April 1. Sea The Stars filly. Half-sister to 3 winners, including smart winner up to 17f The Euphrates and useful 1¼m-1½m winner Modus Operandi. Of obvious interest on debut.

300,000Y Lope de Vega filly who was sent off at odds-on but could only run to a similar level as on debut when third of 9 in novice at Yarmouth (7f, good) last month. Will be suited by this step up to 1m and remains with

races.name: Irishinjuredjockeys.com Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: BARBAPAPA and Rappell are both potentially well treated returned to polytrack with the former getting the vote from a much lower draw. Iff In Doubt was a big disappointment when well backed last time but could be worth another chance back from a break.

runners.note: Mixed record on turf this season but he's better on this surface and is potentially well handicapped back on it. Has to be of interest at this level.
Veteran who ended a long losing run over C&D last month and backed it up when third at Bellewstown 9 days ago. Another 5 lb rise makes him look vulnerable, though.
Maiden winner here (6f) last winter. Hasn't gone on in handicaps this season, though.

Won back-to-back over C&D last winter and returned to winning ways at Bellewstown in April. Generally struggled since but latest fifth at Gowran off sliding mark was at least a step back in the right direction. Usual hea
Yet to win a race but ultra consistent and probably stretched under the conditions when upped in trip at Galway latest. Headgear back on.

Thirsk maiden winner last summer but 0-8 in handicaps for David O'Meara after. Well held on yard debut but fared a lot better when third over C&D 3 weeks ago despite taking a strong hold. Entitled to come on again.
Maiden with a mixed record on the Flat and over hurdles for this yard. Takes a marked drop in trip.
Opened his account for the year at Limerick (6.7f) in July. Decent placed efforts last 2 starts and won here (6f) last autumn off 5 lb higher.
C&D maiden winner in February who posted easily his best effort since when second in a 1m claimer at same course in May. However, has struggled in handicaps otherwise.

Proving expensive to follow for current yard, runner-up 3 times this summer. Not so good the last twice, albeit he was held up in a steadily-run race at Cork last time. Back down in trip on only his second start on all-w

Showed improved form at this course last winter, opening account over C&D in February. Good second here (1m) the following month before running well on turf when fifth of 20 at the Curragh. Major let-down back on this su
No form for current yard.
Had a good spell here last winter but has struggled for form since, including when well backed returned to this venue last 2 starts.
No better than mid-division in 3 maidens and similar story in handicaps. First start in 10 months having left Dermot Weld.
Of little account nowadays. RESERVE.

races.name: Unibet More Extra Place Races Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
races.verdict: Both KINETIC IMPACT and Sin City have layoffs to overcome but they are in very capable hands, with the former marginally preferred. Thornthwaite could emerge as the pick of the newcomers and also needs factoring in.

runners.note: 200,000 gns Too Darn Hot colt. Made a winning start on Lingfield all-weather debut in February and built on that with a very good fifth of 9 in conditions stakes over C&D following month. Off 6 months but can't be ruled
Progressive Frankel colt who posted a very good fourth of 9 on his handicap debut at Southwell (1m) 17 days ago. The form pick back in novice company.
€60,000 yearling, Invincible Spirit colt. Half-brother to French 6.7f winner Blazing Spirit. Dam winner up to 1m (2-y-o 7f winner). The market can guide for this newcomer.
Promising Havana Grey gelding. Fourth of 11 in novice at Windsor (1m, good to soft) on debut in June. Can improve after a break.

Toronado gelding. Brother to 7.6f winner Wedgewood Sapphire and half-brother to 3 winners, including French 6f-9f winner French Pegasus. Dam lightly raced. The betting can prove an accurate indicator.
Fair maiden who posted a solid third of 4 in maiden at Salisbury (1m, good) in July. Big player if returning from a layoff at that level on polytrack debut (has been gelded).
Coulsty gelding. Seventh of 10 in maiden at Lingfield (1m, all-weather) on debut 53 days ago. Needs to build on it.
Well held both runs, coming in last of 5 in novice at Windsor (1m, good) 25 days ago.

£30,000 yearling, Havana Grey gelding. Brother to useful 2-y-o 6f/6.5f winner Panama, and half-brother to 1m winner Blue Artemis and Saudi Arabian 1m winner Maybury. A considered newcomer, especially if the market vibes
Son of Kingman who went with little encouragement when down the field in novice (40/1) at Kempton (1m) on debut 65 days ago. Gelded since.
Workforce mare. Dam, 9f-2m winner, also won over hurdles. Doesn't appeal as a probable first-time-out winner on paper.
Yet to show any promise, visored when last of 6 in maiden at Lingfield (7f, all-weather) last time on final run for Robbie Llewellyn. Tongue strap goes on for the first time for new yard.

races.name: Irishinjuredjockeys.com Handicap (Div 2)
races.verdict: UNA MATATA has been given a chance by the handicapper here and now back at her favoured track she looks the way to go. Boston Max also has winning form here and could prove the chief threat on the back of a solid fourth here after a break, while Mehman and Thaloria also need factoring in.

runners.note: C&D winner. 5/1, respectable eighth of 14 in handicap at Down Royal (7f, good to soft) 11 days ago. Can make his presence felt.
C&D winner. Arrives below par, seventh of 9 in handicap at Killarney (1m, good) last time. Needs to take a step forward.
On a long losing sequence but this 4-time course winner posted a good third of 13 in handicap here (6f) 14 days ago. Considered.
Got off the mark over C&D in January. Back to form with fourth of 14 in handicap at Down Royal (7f, good to soft) 11 days ago. Possibilities.
C&D winner last October. Good fourth over 1m here in March but well below par in a pair of 1m handicaps at the Curragh subsequently. More is needed after a break.
Lightly-raced maiden. Off 11 months/first run since leaving Ger Lyons when tenth of 14 in 6f maiden claimer here 2 weeks ago. Lots more required on handicap debut.
Lightly-raced maiden. Failed to build on earlier promise when thirteenth of 18 on handicap debut at Cork (1m, soft, 20/1) 30 days ago. Not written off.

Good second in 7f Epsom maiden last July for Gary & Josh Moore. Has twice failed to repeat it though, last of 12 in handicap at Gowran (7f, good to soft) in June on sole outing for Ross O'Sullivan. Gelded ahead of return
Finally off the mark in 7f claimer at Gowran in August on final outing for Gerard Keane. Below form in 3 starts for this yard, though, so has it to prove now.

A 3-time C&D winner early in 2026. Hinted at a revival with fifth over C&D in September but well held in handicap at Down Royal (7f, good to soft) 11 days ago. Not without interest back here though off a reduced mark.
Course winner (5f) in April and followed up at Chepstow (5f) in May. Off 11 weeks, not disgraced with fourth of 13 in 6f handicap here 14 days ago. Should strip sharper here and needs considering.

Fair juvenile maiden for Ken Condon. Well held in a pair of  8.5f handicaps on soft ground at Galway for new yard this summer. Makes polytrack debut. Could still do better for good yard, especially if the market vibes ar
Tongue strap on for first time and best run in handicaps when fifth of 13 here (6f) 14 days ago. Needs to build on it.

Opened his account over C&D in November. Good third over C&D (first-time cheekpieces) in February. Well held on turf after a 6 months off last 2 runs but no surprise to see him bounce back here in fist time blinkers.

races.name: Try Unibet's Superboosts Handicap (Div 1)
races.verdict: This looks wide open but it could be worth siding with dual C&D scorer HAVANA TOUCH who wasn't at his best in the mud at Ayr last time and can bounce back in style here with Billy Loughnane now up. A La Noche remains handily weighted and could emerge as the main danger, although Valentine Boy is another to consider returned to his optimum trip.

runners.note: Temperamental sort but he doubled his tally for the season at Epsom (8.5f) in September. Solid fifth of 10 in handicap at Brighton (1m, good) 11 days ago. Not discounted.

Lightly-raced 5-y-o who got off the mark at Salisbury (1m) in September. Ran poorly when eleventh of 12 in handicap at Newmarket (1m, good to firm, 7/2) 15 days ago but not written off on polytrack debut.
Made all twice at Wolverhampton in January. Has failed to beat a rival at Salisbury and Chester on his last 2 runs though. Bounce back is required.
In excellent form on all-weather at the start of the year with 3 wins. Well held on his last 3 runs though, off 4 months before last of 6 in handicap at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) in July.

Gained a second C&D win of 2026 in June. Good second at Lingfield (1m, all-weather) next time but well held on soft ground at Ayr (1m) 22 days ago. Remains one to be interested in back here with Billy Loughnane in the sa
Fourteen runs since his last win in 2024 and he came in a below-form eighth of 13 in handicap over C&D 30 days ago. This course winner needs to take a step forward.
Still a maiden but in good nick until coming in last of 12 in handicap at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) 15 days ago. Needs to bounce back.
Doubled her tally on second run for new yard at Brighton in August but well held both subsequent runs at Chepstow and over C&D 16 days ago. Has a bit to prove now.
Made all at Epsom (8.5f) in August but ridden too aggressively when seventh of 9 there (8.5f, good) 29 days ago. This course winner can bounce back after a break.
Notched a second C&D success in May. Not at his best of late tried over 11f, a free-going sixth of 9 here last time. Not discounted now reverted in trip.
Still seeking her first win but not disgraced after 6 months off when fifth over 11f here and seemed unsuited by the mud when well held at Goodwood since. No forlorn hope.

races.name: BAR 1 Betting 'First For Football' Handicap
races.verdict: BOOYEA needs to shrug off a couple of poor efforts but he was fourth off 7 lb higher in the Irish Cambridgeshire only 3 starts back and he's back down in class. Unexposed 4-y-os Naoi and Hellorhighwater head the dangers.

runners.note: Lightly raced but useful at best for Charlie Appleby. Picked up for £64,000 by this yard but hasn't shown much in 2 runs for them.

Progressive form in maidens for Gavin Cromwell last season, getting off the mark at Cork. Successful return for new stable at Limerick in April and this is easier than the Irish Cambridgeshire he contested on his only st

On a lengthy losing run but went close in a competitive handicap at the Curragh and made the frame in the Irish Cambridgeshire this summer. Seems to have gone off the boil but handicapper has given him a chance back down
Career best when winning at Navan 5 weeks ago. 4 lb rise looks perfectly fair and he's effective on all-weather.
Returned from 4 months off with success here (7f) in March. Mixed record on turf since but he's lurking on a dangerous mark returned to this surface after a break.
Wide-margin winner over C&D around this time last year and responded well to headgear when doubling his tally at Leopardstown in June. Held form well since so player once again.
Resumed winning ways here (7f) in January off 1 lb higher but it's been a mixed bag since, tried in this headgear/tongue strap combination last time.

Much improved for new yard this season after over a year off, winning 2 of her 3 starts, including when beating 17 rivals in good style at Fairyhouse 18 days ago. Remains unexposed (unraced on all-weather) so a must for
Made a winning debut over 7f here last November before showing better form in defeat next 2 starts the following month. Off since and tongue strap applied for this handicap debut. Market can guide.
Highly tried after winning Naas handicap in May last year. Made much more of an impact returned to a more suitable level when third of 5 here (7f) last week.
In good heart when winning back-to-back over C&D in March. Below par both starts on turf this summer but he seems more at home here.

Struggled for consistency with previous trainer but won an 18-runner handicap at Cork (40/1) 30 days ago on second start back with this yard, proving herself at the trip under a positive ride. Up 5 lb in much better race
Dual C&D winner in this headgear last autumn. In good form this summer but last 2 starts were poor. Cheekpieces go back on.
Built on solid debut form to get off the mark in C&D maiden in April but hasn't kicked on from that since for all he's had excuses on occasion, tried in headgear latest.
Good placed efforts here early this year but has hindered his chances at the start since. Off 5 months. RESERVE.
Course winner but struggling for form at present. Potentially well treated back on this surface, though. RESERVE.
Some good efforts here this year but record suggests he's better over 7f. RESERVE.

races.name: Try Unibet's Superboosts Handicap (Div 2)
races.verdict: Lots with chances but GUNFIGHTER looks the way to go given he did well to get up over C&D last time and now has the services of Billy Loughnane for the first time. It'sneverjustone is next on the list after taking a step back in the right direction with his recent Ayr fifth, while Asteverdi and The Hare Rail also need factoring into this open-looking handicap.

runners.note: Winless since 2024 but she posted a good third of 13 to Gunfighter in handicap over C&D 30 days ago. Not out of things.
Dual 7f/1m winner for Denis Quinn last August. Made a positive start for current yard but below form of late, sixth of 12 at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) 15 days ago. Bounce back is needed.

Completed 7f handicap double at the Galway Festival last summer. Yet to add to that in 2026 but hinted at a revival with fifth of 12 in handicap at Ayr (1m, soft) 22 days ago. One to consider with blinkers added for the
Doubled his tally for the season in 12-runner handicap at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) 15 days ago. Up 3 lb but this C&D scorer needs considering.

All 4 wins on all-weather, and he resumed winning ways in 13-runner handicap over C&D 30 days ago, doing well given he conceded first run. Up 3 lb but merits serious consideration with Billy Loughnane up.
C&D winner but on a losing run and he came in well held over C&D last time. Cheekpieces go on for the first time now.
Finally got off the mark in 10-runner handicap at Wolverhampton (8.5f) 18 days ago, just holding on. Can go well again despite a 4 lb weight rise.
Opened her account in novice over C&D in April but has failed to kick on sent handicapping, just a respectable fifth of 10 over C&D 16 days ago. Bit more is needed if she's to double her tally.

A 3-time winner (including over C&D) in 2025. Yet to hit top form this season despite a slipping mark, posting a respectable fourth of 10 in handicap at Bath (1m, good to soft) last time. Needs to step forward.
Ended a losing sequence at Newmarket (1m) in June. Well below par both runs since though, too free when eighth of 12 there (1m) 15 days ago.

races.name: View Restaurant At Dundalk Stadium Apprentice Handicap (0-60)
races.verdict: AITEALL is less exposed than most of these and Joseph O'Brien's 3-y-o can go one better than he did at Down Royal 11 days ago. The consistent Storm Eric and recent C&D runner-up Jazz Forever are also shortlisted.

runners.note: Bounced back to best when winning 1½m claimer at Tramore in July and good second in a similar race at Killarney (1m, good) next time. Quickly back to form when third of 18 in handicap at the Curragh (1¼m, heavy, 12/1) 12

Dual winner on all-weather in the UK. Hasn't kicked on from her win at Leopardstown in April, though shaped as back in form after a very slow break when fifth of 14 in handicap (50/1) at this C&D 21 days ago. Issues at t

Below his best since winning a 0-60 at C&D in January (still sole success) and was only seventh of 10 in claimer (16/1) at Laytown (6f) 29 days ago. Significantly back up in trip. First run for yard after leaving Cian Hu
Course winner who had been running consistently here this season, outside the frame only once from 9 Flat outings. Likely to go well again.
Latest win at Roscommon in May. Lower in the weights on all-weather and ran well after some low-key turf efforts when third of 14 in handicap at this C&D (13/2) 21 days ago. Enters calculations.
Maiden in both codes who was a creditable fourth at Tramore on last Flat start but soundly beaten in maiden hurdles both starts since. Others preferred with cheekpieces reapplied.
Improved in first-time cheekpieces when second of 14 in handicap at Down Royal (11f, good to soft, 18/1) 11 days ago. Bumped into a progressive rival there and he can go well again after 2 lb rise.
Maiden who was holding form well on all-weather prior to Christmas but seems to completely lost her way in 2026.
Offered little in 3 maidens at 7f/1m and now switches to handicap company over longer trip. Tongue strap goes on for first time.
Sole success came over C&D in April 2024. Close third in this grade at Navan in June and returned to form after several lesser efforts when second of 14 in handicap (16/1) at this C&D 21 days ago.
Sent off at long odds and well beaten in 3 maidens. More will be required on handicap debut.
Shaped quite well when eighth of 12 in handicap at Navan (1m) but failed to build on that promise when mid-field over 1¼m there last month. Makes polytrack debut.
Made the frame for just the second time when fourth of 14 in handicap at this course (1½m, 100/1) 14 days ago but will probably need more again if she's to go closer here.
Consistent performer on the all-weather for Charlie Johnston last winter. Largely struggled on turf for current connections and fared no better returned all-weather at C&D 3 weeks ago.
Remains with one standout effort when eighth of 20 in a 6f Curragh maiden and was down the field in a 1m Bellewstown handicap last week. Engaged 2.26 Thurles Thursday. RESERVE.
Three-time C&D winner but nothing to shout about of late. RESERVE.
Infrequent winner who has been operating below his best on all-weather/turf in recent starts. Others more persuasive. Engaged 3.01 Thurles Thursday. RESERVE.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Improved Acca Boosts Handicap
races.verdict: None of these can be ruled out but at the likely odds STAR TIME is worth siding with to build on the promise of his Haydock sixth and resume winning ways. Hat-trick seeking Meet Me In Meraki rates the obvious threat, while Mountbatten and Sahm Naif need considering.

runners.note: Made a bright start for current yard, recording a hat-trick on the all-weather in January/February. In decent nick since until beating only one home (in first-time cheekpieces) at Sandown (1¼m, good) in July. Can bounce
Resumed winning ways at Brighton in May and largely in good form since, fourth of 7 in handicap there (1½m, good) 11 days ago. Not out of things.

Successful twice in 2024. Off 14 months but back in good nick, catching the eye when sixth of 12 in handicap at Haydock (11.5f, heavy) last time when making his effort earlier than ideal. One to be interested in.
Back in fine form and bids for a hat-trick following handicap wins at Chester (1¼m) and Southwell (11f) last month, overcoming a pace bias on latter occasion. Player.

Got off the mark on handicap debut at Southwell in June. Cheekpieces on for first time when a very good Leicester second in August but too free when last of 6 in handicap at Lingfield (13f, all-weather) since. Not writte

Off 10 months before shedding her maiden tag at Salisbury in July. Just denied at Brighton next time but went back to going lethargically in first-time headgear when only fifth there since. Could bounce back with headgea
Dual winner in early summer and has continued in good nick, fifth of 12 in handicap at Wolverhampton (9.5f) 24 days ago. Not one to dismiss.
Lightly-raced maiden who took a step forward when fourth of 9 in handicap at Ffos Las (1¼m, good) in August. Possibilities eased 1 lb.

races.name: Halloween Mid-Term Racing At Dundalk Handicap
races.verdict: CAMINO LAD hasn't looked back since the blinkers went on and can quickly resume winning ways on the back of an excellent recent second here with this step up in trip also a likely plus. Adrian McGuiness' new recruit Serenity Blue could emerge as the main danger, especially if the market vibes are positive, although Showyoutheropes has slipped in the weights and also commands plenty of respect for

runners.note: Easy winner at Leopardstown (9f) in July. Wasn't disgraced off 5 lb higher mark when sixth of 10 at the Curragh last time and one to consider eased 2 lb.

Landed a pair of 1¼m novices last summer. Back to form in cheekpieces when fourth at Doncaster (1¼m) and Chepstow (1m) last 2 runs for James Horton. Interesting recruit for new yard here. Worth a market check.

On the up since fitted with blinkers, getting off the mark in 1m Bellewstown maiden in August before an excellent clear second on handicap debut here (1¼m) 2 weeks ago. A player stepped up further in trip.
Fourteen runs since last win in 2022 but back on track after 4 months off with fifth of 10 in handicap over C&D 21 days ago. Can build on it here.
Opened his account at Leopardstown in July and largely in good form since, third of 14 in handicap at Down Royal (13f, good to soft) 11 days ago. Much respected on polytrack debut.
Lightly-raced maiden. Has failed to build on Flat debut third at Roscommon in June, only seventh of 11 in maiden here 3 weeks ago. Handicap debutant.
A fair winner for Tom Clover in 2025. Below form of late, tenth of 14 in handicap at Down Royal last time. Has slipped to a good mark though and worth a market check with yard going well.

races.name: Try Unibet's New Smartview Racecards Handicap
races.verdict: BOLD SHOUT caught the eye when an unlucky-in-running fourth at Southwell on his first all-weather run and is taken to build on it and make a winning start on polytrack. Course scorer Red Hat Eagle is feared most on the back of a good Thirsk third, while Strong Voice and Majestic Wave need considering too.

runners.note: A 4-time C&D winner but it's now twelve runs since his last win in 2024. Thirteenth of 14 in handicap over C&D in May so has work to do now.
Fourteen runs since last win in 2024 but in good nick, not enjoying a smooth passage when third of 12 in handicap at Thirsk (7f, good, 7/2) 25 days ago. This course winner can make his presence felt.

Signed off with 6f win at Haydock for Dr Richard Newland & Jamie Insole in April. Well held all 3 runs for new yard, eighth of 10 in handicap at Wolverhampton (6f) 21 days ago, eased down. Cheekpieces go on for first tim
Twice runner-up in handicaps here (latest over C&D) in August but below par both runs since, seventh of 10 in handicap at Wolverhampton (6f) 21 days ago. Bounce back is needed.
Dual winner over 1m here. Yet to hit top form this season, off 6 months before a fading tenth of 14 in handicap over C&D 30 days ago. Can take a step forward now.
Won 7f Newcastle handicap in March. Off 5 months but posted a good second of 9 in handicap at Southwell (7f) 15 days ago. Much respected on his polytrack debut.

Got off the mark in 6f novice at Salisbury in August. Caught the eye on his all-weather debut when fourth of 9 in 7f handicap at Southwell 15 days ago, finishing well having been hampered over 1f out. Makes polytrack deb
Has a very good all-weather record and gained a third 7f Lingfield win in September. Sent off evens, she was just a fair fourth of 9 in 7f handicap there last time. Considered.
Still a maiden but runner-up for the third time this season in 8-runner handicap at Lingfield (7f, all-weather) 27 days ago, clear of rest. Must enter calculations.
Made a winning debut at Newcastle (6f) last November. However, she hasn't built on it this year, seventh of 10 in handicap here (1m) 25 days ago. Others more persuasive.
Got off the mark at Windsor (6f) in May but rather in and out since, only eighth of 11 in handicap at Leicester (6f, good) 31 days ago. Cheekpieces go on for first time now.
Ended a long losing sequence in 10-runner handicap at Lingfield (7f, all-weather) last month, holding on gamely. Up 3 lb but should remain competitive.

Successful twice at Wolverhampton last spring for Simon & Ed Crisford. However, he ended his time with that yard on a low-key note and it's been a similar story in 5 starts for new connections this summer. Hooded for fir
Unreliable sort but he gained a second success of 2026 at Leicester in July. Went with little fluency though when ninth of 12 in handicap at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last time.

races.name: Christmas Party Nights At Dundalk Handicap
races.verdict: Claims can be made for all 5 but FIXATION looks the most progressive one and he did well when switched to this surface last year. Tribal Star is next best.

Did well here last winter and has taken his form to another level this year, winning at the Curragh and Gowran. Decent effort when mid-field in Premier Handicap at former track last time and this trip probably more suita
Useful 11f winner for George Scott and gained a first success for his current yard here (1¼m) in August. Bit too keen for his own good at Doncaster since.

Has produced some creditable efforts in defeat in some good staying races this season. Losing run is building but remains on a good mark and this is less competitive than what he's been contesting lately.

Has largely struggled this summer but capitalised on a falling mark here (11f) 2 weeks ago, the return to all-weather probably the key. Remains potentially well treated despite being 2 lb out of the weights here.
